purpose: define how attached acoustic boundary models contribute mode-dependent damping in the current rectangular analytical solver without inferring physics from semantic treatment type

materialProfileExtension.definition: dimensionless dissipative part of normalized surface admittance, Re(rho*c/Zs), used only by the current impedance damping approximation

lossRules: only an AcousticObject with a RoomSurfaceAttachment may contribute rectangular-room boundary loss
rigid and scattering models contribute zero damping in this solver
absorptive model loss uses the existing absorption-coefficient approximation
impedance model loss uses normalized surface conductance directly
semantic object type such as absorber, diffuser or bass-trap must never select a solver formula
free-standing treatment contributes zero room-boundary loss in the current rectangular solver
wall treatment changes modal damping only and must not attenuate unobstructed direct sound

modalWeight.effectiveBoundaryArea: integral approximation of attachment area weighted by squared modal pressure and rectangular modal normalization

impedanceApproximationLimits: the current solver consumes only the dissipative real conductance term
reactive surface susceptance and impedance-driven modal-frequency shift are not yet solved
this is a perturbative modal-damping approximation, not an exact mixed-impedance eigenmode solution
normalizedConductance values must be explicit profile data; they must not be synthesized from the semantic object type inside the solver
generic idealized profiles are allowed only when clearly identified as idealized rather than measured manufacturer data
regressions: an attached absorptive treatment reduces response at a modal antinode
the same treatment produces less damping where the covered boundary patch is weak for that mode
an attached impedance treatment with non-zero normalized conductance increases modal inverse-Q
free-standing treatment produces zero rectangular boundary loss
scattering treatment does not fake damping
direct field is unchanged by wall treatment
